To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CRCM performs well at simulating the marginal values and bivariate joint occurrence probabilities of flood characteristics for northeastern Canadian basins and the future marginal values and bivariant joint occurrence probabilities of these flood characteristics are likely to increase.

the Canadian regional climate model performs well in simuling current flood characteristics and their joint occurrence probabilities, and the future values of these quantities are projected to increase.

(a) the CRCM can simulate the current (1971–2000) flood characteristics and their univariate and bivaraite frequency distributions well; (b) the projected changes to flood statistics, in general, are consistent with those obtained in other parts of Canada and the world; (c) the projected changes in the joint occurrence probabilities are more significant than those in the marginal values of flood statistics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comprehensive assessment of the CRCM in simulating flood characteristics and the bivariate joint occurrence probabilities for the current and future periods.
the assessment of the CRCM performance and its projected climate change impact on flood characteristics and their joint occurrence probabilities.
the evaluation of the performance of the Canadian regional climate model in reproducing the observed flood characteristics and their bivariate joint occurrence probabilities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future marginal and joint values of flood characteristics are expected to increase, but the magnitude of change is not clear due to uncertainties.

the CRCM is capable of simulating flood characteristics and their joint occurrence probabilities well for the current and future periods and that the CRCM simulated future changes in the flood characteristics and their occurrence probabilities are realistic.
the CRCM simulations indicate that anthropogenic climate change will have significant impacts on flood characteristics in northeastern Canada.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the CRCM performs well for simulating the flood characteristics and the copula based bivariates for the present period.

the copula based bivariant analysis provides an efficient way to assess the impact of climate change on flood characteristics, and it is a useful tool for the development of flood risk management strategies.

the CRCM performs well for the present climate in simulating flood characteristics and the joint occurrence of flood characteristics and can be used for the assessment of climate change impact on flood characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the copula-based bivariate approach is a better way to assess climate change impacts on flood characteristics than univariate approach, because it provides more information about the future joint occurrence probability of flood characteristics.
the bivariate copula-based analysis is an effective and useful approach for assessing the joint effects of anthropogenic climate change on flood characteristics.
the copula based bivaraite frequency analysis is a powerful and flexible approach for assessing the climate change impacts on flood characteristics and their joint occurrence probabilities.
